messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary group 'wave-7' exceeded latency SLO (p50 ~ 120ms -> 420ms, p99 spike). Automated pager triggered. Rollout id: r-2026-03-17-7cb2.

alex (oncall): seeing the pager. checking dashboards. any immediate customer escalations?

mike (eng-runtime): I can see kernel fallback events in the canary logs — devices falling back to scalar kernels around 16:42 UTC. Batching lookups show microbatch size collapse to 1 in a subset of pods.

jen (sre): perf metrics: throughput down ~28% for canary, error rate slightly up (0.2% -> 0.6%). No 5xx surge, just tail latency.

alex (oncall): ok, what's the rolling change? Paul, you own the release?

paul (eng-releases): yes — wave-7 flipped a quant-path selector and a small prefetch tweak. Should be backwards-compatible. Deployment: canary at 10% traffic.

mike (eng-runtime): breakdown: quant selector is triggering a new kernel codepath for certain model sharding patterns. Kernel fallback appears when batch headroom is low and sequence lengths vary. We also see KV cache churn; prefetch may be thrashing.

jen (sre): impact calc: ~2.3% of total requests routed to canary. For affected slice, p99 latency went from 580ms -> 1.8s. Potential customer-facing tail.

kara (cs): no direct CS tickets yet but monitoring for customer-visible errors. if rollback happens, notify key customers (Acme, Flowly).

alex (oncall): mitigation plan? Options: a) toggle release flag to route away from canary; b) flip feature kill-switch for quant path; c) rollback canary. Which is fastest?

mike (eng-runtime): fastest is kill-switch for quant selector (feature flag ff/quant-path) — we can flip in <60s and it unroutes the new kernel path. Routing away from canary requires rollout flip which takes ~2-5m to propagate.

paul (eng-releases): I'll prepare rollback if kill-switch doesn't stabilize.

alex (oncall): do it. mike, flip ff/quant-path now and watch.

mike (eng-runtime): flipping ff/quant-path :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: Feature flag change applied by mike at 16:46:23 UTC (ff/quant-path=false).

mike (eng-runtime): initial metrics: p50 down to 150ms, p99 dropping back to 620ms within 90s. KV cache miss rate stabilizing. Looks promising.

jen (sre): monitor for 10 minutes, then decide if rollback unnecessary. Also capturing logs for postmortem.

alex (oncall): Kara, keep customers notified: "we detected elevated latency during a canary; we've disabled the new quant selector and are monitoring."

kara (cs): sending brief to customer SLAs now.

paul (eng-releases): rolling back held in reserve but standing down for now. I will not initiate full rollback while kill-switch is performing.

mike (eng-runtime): hypothesis: the quant-selector change changed kernel codepath selection heuristics causing a mismatch with batch-shaping heuristics under real traffic. Prefetch tweak amplified KV churn, lowering effective batching and forcing scalar fallback on some GPUs.

jen (sre): action items captured: (1) collect kernel selector traces (mike), (2) add auto-rollback safety check to release pipeline if p99 > 1s for >2m (paul), (3) postmortem with RCA and remediation (alex leads).

alex (oncall): leaving a note for follow-up: I'll handoff to night oncall in 45m. If p99 creeps above 900ms again, escalate to ENG-Runtime.

mike (eng-runtime): saving logs and trace links: https://internal.monitoring/reports/r-2026-03-17-7cb2/kernels (private).

paul (eng-releases): adding a gating check to the release: require canary p99 < 800ms for 10m before wave propagation.

kara (cs): customers notified: "we mitigated the issue and disabled the new selector; we will follow up with root cause and timeline for re-deploy."

alex (oncall): summary for incident record: cause suspected kernel-path mismatch due to quant selector + prefetch tweak -> batching collapse -> kernel fallback -> tail latency. Mitigation: feature flag flip (ff/quant-path=false) succeeded. No rollback needed. Customer impact: small tail latency for ~2.3% requests, no data loss. Next steps: RCA and gating.

jen (sre): I'll create an incident ticket and assign RCA to eng-runtime. Alex will lead.

alex (oncall): handing off to night oncall @sam in 45m — leaving current state: stable, monitoring at normal levels, watchlist onwave-7 and kg-p99.

sam (night-oncall): ack will monitor.

paul (eng-releases): note: we'll hold off re-enabling ff/quant-path until after changes to batching heuristics are validated in a staging perf run.

mike (eng-runtime): agreed — I'll prototype kernel selector guard and prefetch rate limiter.

alex (oncall): closing pager for now. If anything regresses, reopen thread or page ENG-Runtime. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
